name: Musée National Barthélemy Boganda
subtitle: National ethnographic museum preserving Central African musical traditions, Pygmy material culture, and founding history.

facts.label: Building
facts.value: Former colonial residence of Barthélemy Boganda

facts.label: Collections
facts.value: Ubangian and Aka Pygmy musical instruments, pottery, hunting gear, and ritual masks

parts.text: The national ethnographic museum of the Central African Republic, located in the 2nd arrondissement of Bangui in the historic villa that served as the home of Barthélemy Boganda, the anti-colonial leader and founding father of the nation. Opened in 1966, the museum safeguards irreplaceable ethnographic collections representing the diverse ethnic cultures of the Ubangi basin, including Aka and BaAka Pygmy material arts, harp-zithers, sanza thumb pianos, ritual terracotta, and royal regalia.
